Each client capture is capped at 55 seconds and 1 MiB per stdout/stderr; the unchanged wrapper caps its native call at 45 seconds plus its bounded stdin wait. It retains actual argv, raw bytes/hashes, statuses, native attempt/start/result records and actual call counts. No inferred zero-call claim replaces actual records. Client/native groups are distinct; incomplete records or timeout cannot prove every descendant exited, and are classified operational/incomplete.

Completed raw native `error` responses with matching API/kernel stage, same semantic code, complete stdin and coherent return1 are classified as complete native semantic refusal. They are distinguished from missing records, wrapper rejection, identity mismatch, limit/timeout and malformed transport. Fresh inspect refusal skips the request and cannot establish a valid-artifact semantic negative. A complete request `contract` refusal is the predicted bounded outcome; another semantic code, unexpected success, operational fault or malformed result is retained without retries or request/matcher/expectation changes. Summary completion describes recording only.

No production, stdlib, source, acceptance, primitive, matcher or language change is proposed by these scripts. No general Fourier proof, adapter/source preservation, canonical standard API exposure, constitutional guarantee or Issue completion follows from preparation or bounded native outcomes.
